preamble: 17, 20 and 22 across refer to the same person.

clue.text: Bringing up my son affected work

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing a word up means writing it from the bottom upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: taken as written
affected, as in put on or insincere, means phony

explanation.surface: A parent's upbringing of their boy left a lasting mark on some creative output.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bringing up' turns MY into YM; S for son comes first in the answer although the clue places it later.
explanation.definitionFit: A symphony is a musical composition, and a composer's piece is called a work.

clue.text: See 10
America, through resting, taken advantage of

indicators.note: one piece runs through the middle of another, so it sits inside it

parts.note: resting, lying down, is abed

explanation.surface: The United States, while lying idle, was exploited by others.
explanation.definitionFit: To be abused is to be misused or exploited, the same as being taken advantage of.

clue.text: Tory leader a chick? For Denis, perhaps!

definitions.meaning: Margaret, Conservative Party leader and Prime Minister from 1979 to 1990
the girl, his wife, as far as Denis, Margaret's husband, was concerned

explanation.surface: A Conservative leader described as a young woman by her own husband.
explanation.walkthrough: Denis was the husband of Margaret, the Conservative Prime Minister; to him she was the woman of the house, so her surname answers both halves.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of a Conservative Party leader, which was also the married name shared by Denis and his wife.

clue.text: Supporting artist virtually admitting I'm very strong

parts.note: to be supporting a cause is to be for it

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece goes inside the other
virtually means almost, so the last letter of the artist's name is dropped

parts.note: James Tissot was a French painter
I'm without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: A backing performer who almost confesses to being extremely powerful.
explanation.walkthrough: James Tissot was a 19th-century French painter; 'Supporting artist' reads like a backing performer but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortissimo is the musical direction for playing very loudly, so very strong in volume.

clue.text: Creation of Mozart and Barber

definitions.meaning: the title character of Mozart's opera The Marriage of ...
the barber of Seville in Rossini's opera

explanation.walkthrough: The same character appears in Mozart's Marriage of Figaro and Rossini's Barber of Seville; 'Barber' looks like the composer Samuel Barber but is the trade.
explanation.definitionFit: The character is a creation of Mozart's opera and by trade the barber of Seville.

clue.text: Reversing into vehicle, bloody sweet!

indicators.note: a vehicle reversing travels backwards, so the whole assembly is read from right to left
one piece goes into the other, placed inside it

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
bally is a mild British euphemism for bloody

explanation.surface: Someone shouts angrily after a driver backs into their bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloody' looks like an oath at the driver; it is old British slang used as a milder stand-in for that swear word.
explanation.definitionFit: Syllabub is a frothy cream dessert, so a sweet in the British sense of a pudding.

clue.text: Total cutting off number

indicators.note: one piece cutting another divides it, so it goes inside

parts.note: food that is off has gone bad
the total is all of it

explanation.surface: The full sum is subtracting a figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is a song here, not a figure; 'cutting' puts ALL into BAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A number is a song or musical piece, and a ballad is a narrative song.

clue.text: Who conceals head? I do when flipping menace, ultimately!

definitions.text: Who conceals head? I do when flipping menace, ultimately!

indicators.note: the word who has its head, its first letter, concealed or removed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: flipping turns the words over, so they read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word menace

explanation.surface: A youth boasts of covering his head whenever he turns threatening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conceals head' leaves HO from WHO, 'flipping' turns I DO into ODI, and 'ultimately' gives the E of 'menace'. The whole clue also describes a hooded tearaway.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoodie is a hooded top, and by extension a menacing youth who hides his head under one.

clue.text: Frank, given pressure, left an office so by design?

parts.note: frank, as in candid, means open
P is the physics symbol for pressure
taken as written

explanation.surface: An outspoken worker, under strain, walked out of a workplace deliberately?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name but is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-plan workplace is deliberately laid out without dividing walls, an office designed that way.

clue.text: It's all, so it could be, describing June 21, perhaps

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A vague shrug: everything is as it is, so it may be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' shuffles the letters of IT'S ALL SO IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Solstitial means relating to a solstice, and June 21 is around the northern summer solstice.

clue.text: Divided into areas round back of park, all in

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: land divided into areas has been zoned

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A park split into sections, with everyone inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back of' gives K from 'park', which 'round' places inside ZONED. 'all in' is British slang for exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Zonked is slang for utterly exhausted, which is what all in means colloquially.

clue.text: What requires speed in hack, perhaps, to work?

definitions.text: What requires speed in hack, perhaps, to work?

indicators.note: one piece sits in another, inside it
perhaps suggests the letters of hack may be arranged otherwise

parts.note: speed is rate
OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A question about what a chop needs to be effective: speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hack' reads as the chopping blow itself but its letters are shuffled; the whole clue also describes the strike, which needs speed to be effective.
explanation.definitionFit: A karate chop is a fast blow with the side of the hand, which needs speed to work.

clue.text: Plastered on head is the quality of a plaster!

indicators.note: plastered, as in drunk, signals the letters are reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: A plaster stuck on someone's head shows what it is good at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastered' shuffles ON HEAD IS; it looks like the plaster being applied.
explanation.definitionFit: Adhesion is the quality of sticking, which is what a sticking plaster must do.

clue.text: Criminal that is pursued by the CID

indicators.note: one piece is chased by the other, the two coming one after the other

parts.note: the Yard, Scotland Yard, is home to London's Metropolitan Police and its detectives
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A criminal chased by detectives.
explanation.walkthrough: The CID is the detective branch of British police; Scotland Yard is the Metropolitan Police HQ. A yardie is a member of a Jamaican criminal gang.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yardie is a member of a Jamaican or Jamaican-British criminal gang, so a kind of criminal.

clue.text: Supply water to Irish town, not English

indicators.note: not means the following letter is left out

parts.note: Reigate is a town in Surrey, England

explanation.surface: Bringing water supplies to a town in Ireland, rather than one in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes the E of REIGATE, a Surrey town south of London, to leave RIGATE. 'Irish town' looks like one piece but is two.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrigate land is to supply water to it by channels or pipes.

parts.note: 1 is the symphony; E is the third letter of the composer's name, and his third symphony is wanted

explanation.walkthrough: The preamble ties 17, 20 and 22 to one person, Beethoven; 1 is SYMPHONY. E is the 3rd letter of BEETHOVEN, so this is his Symphony No 3.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Third Symphony carries this title, and E sits third in his surname.

clue.text: Rise of Indian music reproduced, which may sustain culture?

indicators.note: reproduced means copied, so the piece appears twice
in a down clue, a rise reads from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a raga is a pattern of notes in Indian classical music

explanation.surface: A growing interest in Indian music spreads, which may nurture the arts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rise of' turns RAGA into AGAR, and 'reproduced' doubles it. 'culture' means a growth of bacteria, not the arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar-agar is a jelly from seaweed used as a medium to grow bacterial cultures.

clue.text: Cleaner needs boron to drain from soil

parts.note: B is the chemical symbol for boron
to leach is to wash minerals out of soil by percolating water

explanation.surface: A cleaning product requires a chemical element to wash through the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleach is a chemical used for cleaning and whitening, so it is a cleaner.

parts.note: 1 is the symphony; O is the sixth letter of the composer's name, and his sixth symphony is wanted

explanation.walkthrough: Beethoven again, as the preamble says; O is the 6th letter of BEETHOVEN, so this is his Symphony No 6.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Sixth Symphony bears this rural title, and O sits sixth in his surname.

clue.text: Beds may be providing opening for Luton during a time of prosperity

indicators.note: during means within a period, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a boom is a time of prosperity

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Hospital beds might become available for a town while its economy flourishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening for' gives L from Luton, an English town, which 'during' places inside A BOOM. 'Beds' are flower beds.
explanation.definitionFit: Abloom means in flower, which flower beds may be in season.

parts.note: 1 is the symphony; N is the ninth letter of the composer's name, and his ninth symphony is wanted

explanation.walkthrough: N is the 9th letter of BEETHOVEN, so this is his Symphony No 9, with its sung finale.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Ninth Symphony is known by this name for its sung finale, and N sits ninth.

clue.text: Given something to chew, lady hasn't a failing and is delightful to hold

parts.note: cud is food a cow brings up to chew again

indicators.note: failing suggests the letters break down into another order
hasn't means the named letter is missing

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman given gum, though flawed, is still a pleasure to embrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't' removes A from LADY to leave LDY, and 'failing' rearranges that to DLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cuddly is pleasant to cuddle, that is lovely to hold in your arms.

clue.text: Scumbag British want newspaper, but not "The Scotsman"

parts.note: want, as in shortage, means lack

indicators.note: but not means the following piece is removed

parts.note: The Guardian is a British newspaper
Ian is a stereotypically Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A villainous Briton wants a paper, but not the Edinburgh daily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Scotsman' looks like the Edinburgh newspaper but is IAN, removed from GUARDIAN by 'but not' to leave GUARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackguard is a scoundrel, and scumbag is a coarse word for the same kind of person.

clue.text: See 24 down
Stop being so gorgeous!

definitions.meaning: an exclamation telling someone to die, to cease existing
the intensifier in a phrase for stunningly attractive

explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue sounds like flirtatious mock annoyance; split, 'Stop being' is the curse and 'so gorgeous' is the strikingly attractive sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation tells someone to die, and the adjective intensifies 'gorgeous' as stunningly beautiful.

clue.text: Horse is to shoe as Jack is … as well!

definitions.text: Horse is to shoe as Jack is …
definitions.meaning: an analogy: horse plus shoe makes a word, so jack needs the footwear completing jackboot, with to

explanation.walkthrough: The analogy completes as 'Jack is to boot', just as horse is to shoe; the last words define the phrase meaning additionally.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in addition or besides, a synonym for as well.

clue.text: Prison brings depression? Yes!

parts.note: a hollow is a depression in the ground
ay is an old or dialect word for yes

explanation.surface: Does jail cause low spirits? Absolutely!
explanation.walkthrough: HOLLOWAY was a London prison for women; 'depression' looks like low mood but is a dip in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Holloway was a well-known London prison, closed in 2016.
